messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert triggered for routing-api (sev: P1). Metric: cross-region request error rate spike + automated traffic-shift initiated from eu-west-1 -> us-east-1. Pager: @elaine.sre

elaine.sre: Ack, looking. Seeing increased 5xx from eu-west-1 frontends and traffic-shift job kicked off about 30s ago. Can someone confirm whether the automated failover completed or if it's still in progress?

raj.netops: I'm seeing BGP withdraws for a subset of eu-west-1 AZ prefixes, looks like one AZ's eBGP sessions flapped and the cloud infra retried. Cloud provider status shows 'Network instabilities in eu-west-1a' — raising a ticket.

monica.eng: Canary shows that weights were pushed to us-east-1 but connections to the new backends are failing health checks (502/524). LB logs indicate many connections stuck in CLOSE_WAIT on the origin side. Could be stuck draining on the eu side.

elaine.sre: Important: these errors are user-facing for our hosted API (text generation + embeddings). Initial impact estimate: ~15% increased error rate for EU customers, higher tail latency for in-flight requests. Jake, please inform support and surface to affected customers.

jake.support: On it. Posting templated message to customers in affected regions, and adding the incident link. Will escalate one enterprise account that reported timeouts.

raj.netops: TL;DR root cause candidate: partial AZ networking degradation led to inconsistent health propagation. Automated traffic-shift tried to move traffic but session draining on eu targets didn't complete, causing LB to continue sending some traffic to unhealthy backends -> 5xx. Also saw Route Cache entries not updated fast enough in a few edge routers.

elaine.sre: Actions now: 1) Pause automated traffic-shift policy to avoid oscillation. 2) Force immediate connection termination on eu-west frontends to unblock draining. 3) If LB continues to route to unhealthy backends, do manual region failover (dns/route) as fallback.

monica.eng: Working command to force-close connections on the frontends (run on frontier nodes):

```
# kill stuck haproxy connections older than 60s
sudo ss -tanp state CLOSE-WAIT | awk '{print $6}' | xargs -r sudo kill -9
# then force re-check
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:9000/healthz
```

elaine.sre: I'm going to pause the automated router job now.

incident-bot: Job "auto-region-shift" paused by elaine.sre at 1768889975

raj.netops: Cloud-provider-bot: any updates from provider ticket?

cloud-provider-bot: AWS case #123456789 opened. They acknowledge a partial network fabric issue in eu-west-1a. ETA unknown, mitigation in progress on their side.

monica.eng: After forcing connection closes, per-node health checks recovered slowly. However the LB's connection table had stale entries; I triggered an LB reload which cleared those. Post-reload metrics show backend error rate dropping from ~22% -> ~3% in 10 minutes.

elaine.sre: Good. Next: lower DNS TTL for routing CNAMEs to speed manual shift if needed. Raj, can you prepare manual DNS change plan and a rollback? Keep TTL change minimal and doc the exact records.

raj.netops: Preparing plan now. Proposal: lower TTL to 30s on edge CNAMEs, then update DNS to point primary record to us-east-1 ingress IPs only if errors re-spike. Rollback: restore original TTL + revert CNAME to eu endpoints.

jake.support: Customer update posted. One enterprise rep already replied, asking for ETA. I told them we're mitigating and will provide a follow-up in 30 minutes.

elaine.sre: Monitoring closely. Setting an incident bridge in 5. If the error rate stays below 5% for next 20 minutes, we'll move to degrade->monitor. If it creeps back, we'll execute manual DNS shift.

incident-bot: Incident bridge created: https://meet.example.com/incident/1768889999

(20 minutes pass)

monica.eng: Error rate creeping up to ~8% and now steady. Some edge routers still show stale routecache entries after LB reload. I recommend manual DNS shift now to avoid user impact increasing.

elaine.sre: Agreed. Execute manual DNS shift. Raj, execute with Jake on the DNS console.

raj.netops: Executing now: lowering TTL to 30s... done. Updating CNAME to point to us-east-1 ingress pool... done. Propagation check in progress (dig + curl).

```
# sanity check
dig +short edge.example.net
curl -sS https://edge.example.net/health | jq .status
```

monica.eng: Probing shows majority of traffic now landing in us-east-1. Error rate dropping to ~2% within 90s. Good.

jake.support: Updated customer message: failover executed, errors reduced, we continue monitoring. One customer asked for confirmation when eu-west is healthy again.

elaine.sre: Logging this as a controlled manual failover. We'll keep the incident open until provider confirms eu-west1a fabric is healthy and we've validated route stability for 60 minutes. Also capture action items: - tighten guardrails for automated shifts (prevent shifts if draining > threshold) - improve routecache invalidation on edge routers - add runbook step for force-close with safer command wrapper.

incident-bot: Incident severity adjusted to P2 by elaine.sre at 1768890780 (service degraded but manual failover successful).

cloud-provider-bot: AWS updates case: engineers completed repairs in eu-west-1a, network fabric reported stable at 1768892000. Recommend customers validate.

monica.eng: Repointed DNS back to eu endpoints as a test during low traffic window. Health checks green, routecache entries updated. Rolling back TTL to standard value.

elaine.sre: Confirming: we've rolled traffic back to eu-west primary, monitoring for 60 minutes. Leaving this thread open for postmortem notes. Handoff to next on-call: @raja.netops will take L2 watch and file the incident postmortem template.

raj.netops: Taking handoff. I'll collect logs, timeline, and draft postmortem. Key timestamps: alert 1768889999, auto-shift pause 1768889975, manual DNS shift 1768890200, provider repair 1768892000.

jake.support: Support follow-up scheduled and informed affected customers.

elaine.sre: Thanks everyone. Add any additional notes here; we'll close after postmortem review. :white_check_mark:
